devices.description: Follow stored spring energy through the gears to the hands.

parts.name: Case & crystal
parts.simple: The case locates the movement and protects its small clearances.
parts.deep: The case locates the movement and protects its small clearances. The crystal covers the dial while allowing the wearer to read the hands. Seals and a crown interface influence resistance to dust and moisture.
parts.made: The case is machined or formed; a crystal, back, crown and seals are fitted around the movement.

parts.name: Mainspring barrel
parts.simple: Winding stores elastic energy in a long coiled spring.
parts.deep: Winding stores elastic energy in a long coiled spring. The barrel contains it and delivers torque to the train. Spring torque changes as it unwinds; usable reserve depends on friction and the energy demanded by the oscillator.
parts.made: A spring strip is formed and installed in a toothed barrel with an arbor and cover.

parts.name: Going train
parts.simple: A sequence of wheels and pinions reduces rotational speed and transmits energy toward the escapement.
parts.deep: A sequence of wheels and pinions reduces rotational speed and transmits energy toward the escapement. Each mesh reverses the direction of rotation. Tooth counts set ratios; backlash, alignment and lubricant condition influence loss.
parts.made: Wheels and pinions are precision formed and supported between plates and bridges.

parts.name: Dial & hands
parts.simple: The motion work creates the minute and hour rotations.
parts.deep: The motion work creates the minute and hour rotations. The hour hand turns once for twelve minute-hand revolutions. Setting the hands and winding the spring use different paths through the keyless works.
parts.made: Printed or finished dial surfaces and thin formed hands are fitted to concentric shafts.

parts.name: Lever escapement
parts.simple: The escape wheel is locked and released by a pallet mechanism.
parts.deep: The escape wheel is locked and released by a pallet mechanism. Impulses replace energy lost by the balance. This intermittent exchange lets the train advance without allowing the mainspring to discharge freely.
parts.made: An escape wheel, pallet fork and contact surfaces are assembled with controlled engagement geometry.

parts.name: Balance & hairspring
parts.simple: The balance has rotational inertia and the hairspring provides restoring torque.
parts.deep: The balance has rotational inertia and the hairspring provides restoring torque. Their interaction produces an oscillation. Shock, magnetic influence, temperature and spring geometry can change the rate.
parts.made: A balanced wheel, spring and pivots are assembled and adjusted as an oscillator.

parts.name: Crown & winding works
parts.simple: The crown turns a winding or setting mechanism depending on its position.
parts.deep: The crown turns a winding or setting mechanism depending on its position. A clutch redirects the mechanical path. Wear or poor engagement can prevent winding even when the going train remains intact.
parts.made: Small gears, levers, springs and a sliding clutch are retained on the movement plate.

parts.name: Jewelled bearings
parts.simple: Hard smooth bearing surfaces support tiny pivots.
parts.deep: Hard smooth bearing surfaces support tiny pivots. They reduce wear while locating shafts; they do not make the watch frictionless. Endshake, side clearance and lubrication must all suit the assembly.
parts.made: Synthetic bearing jewels are formed, finished and fitted into their supports.

parts.name: Bridges & fasteners
parts.simple: Bridges retain the train above the main plate and maintain shaft alignment.
parts.deep: Bridges retain the train above the main plate and maintain shaft alignment. A displaced bridge can change gear engagement across several wheels at once. Screws and locating features keep the assembly repeatable.
parts.made: Metal bridges are machined, finished, located and secured to the main plate.

parts.name: Rate adjustment
parts.simple: A regulating arrangement changes the oscillator’s effective behaviour.
parts.deep: A regulating arrangement changes the oscillator’s effective behaviour. Rate adjustment is different from restoring power reserve or correcting an incorrectly set hand. The demonstration is a teaching movement, not a servicing tool.
parts.made: Adjustment and retention features are assembled near the balance and checked against timing measurements.

guide.principle: A mechanical watch separates energy storage from timekeeping. The mainspring supplies energy; the going train carries it; the escapement meters the release and maintains the balance oscillation. The hands display the resulting rotation. A periodic oscillator can regulate a changing spring supply, but its rate is still affected by geometry, losses and environment.
guide.design: Gear reduction sets hand speeds, while the oscillator sets the time base. Doubling wheel size without preserving tooth ratios does not automatically preserve timing. A full winding does not guarantee correct rate. The 3D demonstration separates train rotation from the balance motion and slows the mechanism for visibility.
guide.manufacture: Precision plates locate pivots on two sides. Wheels, pinions, bridges, springs and bearings are assembled with very small clearances. Alignment and friction matter throughout the train, and the case must protect those clearances while allowing winding and setting.
guide.diagnosis: A stopped watch can involve depleted energy, blocked gears or oscillator failure. Incorrect displayed time can be a setting error even when the rate is stable. The experiment counts two half-swings per oscillator cycle; it does not predict a particular watch’s accuracy.
guide.equation: Beats per second = 2 × oscillator frequency
guide.history: Mechanical timekeeping developed over centuries through many clockmakers. Seiko’s movement documentation describes modern spring materials and bearing engineering; this original drawing does not reproduce a branded calibre.

experiment.label: Oscillator frequency
experiment.note: Two beats per full oscillation. Ideal count, not an accuracy prediction.

prediction.text: Which assembly stores energy when a mechanical watch is wound?
prediction.answer: Winding stores elastic energy in a long coiled spring. The barrel contains it and delivers torque to the train. Spring torque changes as it unwinds; usable reserve depends on friction and the energy demanded by the oscillator.

devices.description: Explore pistons, valves and the crankshaft in a spark-ignition engine.

parts.name: Cylinder block
parts.simple: The block locates cylinder bores and carries combustion and bearing loads.
parts.deep: The block locates cylinder bores and carries combustion and bearing loads. A bore guides the piston; passages around it can support cooling and lubrication. The cutaway deliberately exposes a representative cylinder rather than a specific engine casting.
parts.made: A block is cast or formed, machined and finished at its bores, deck and bearing seats.

parts.name: Crankshaft & bearings
parts.simple: The crank converts piston and connecting-rod motion into rotation.
parts.deep: The crank converts piston and connecting-rod motion into rotation. Main bearings locate the shaft while offset crankpins carry rod loads. The shaft must resist cyclic bending and torsion as well as transmit useful torque.
parts.made: A shaft is forged or cast, machined, balanced and supported by bearings.

parts.name: Piston & rings
parts.simple: The piston changes the cylinder volume and transmits gas force to the rod.
parts.deep: The piston changes the cylinder volume and transmits gas force to the rod. Rings help control gas leakage and oil distribution. Clearances change with temperature, so a cold geometric fit alone is insufficient.
parts.made: A piston is formed and machined; ring grooves, pins and retaining features are finished and assembled.

parts.name: Cylinder head & chamber
parts.simple: The head closes the bore and retains valves and a spark plug.
parts.deep: The head closes the bore and retains valves and a spark plug. Chamber shape and ports influence gas exchange and combustion. A gasket joins the head to the block while separating gas, coolant and oil paths.
parts.made: The head is formed and machined, then fitted with guides, seats and joining hardware.

parts.name: Connecting rod
parts.simple: The rod joins the piston pin to the crankpin.
parts.deep: The rod joins the piston pin to the crankpin. Its angle changes through the stroke, so piston displacement is not a perfect sine wave. The demonstration uses a slider-crank relation to move the piston and rod together.
parts.made: A rod is formed, machined and fitted at its small and large bearing ends.

parts.name: Intake valve & port
parts.simple: The intake valve opens a path for fresh charge during the intake process.
parts.deep: The intake valve opens a path for fresh charge during the intake process. Valve movement and gas flow are different: pressure differences and port geometry determine how much enters. The drawing omits an actual fuel-system specification.
parts.made: A valve, seat, guide, spring and port are retained in the head.

parts.name: Exhaust valve & port
parts.simple: The exhaust valve releases burned gas during the exhaust process.
parts.deep: The exhaust valve releases burned gas during the exhaust process. Hot gas loads its valve and seat thermally. Closing the valve must restore a sealing interface; a visible port is not an open hole throughout the entire cycle.
parts.made: Heat-resistant valve and seat components are finished and installed in the head.

parts.name: Camshaft & timing drive
parts.simple: A four-stroke cycle takes two crank revolutions.
parts.deep: A four-stroke cycle takes two crank revolutions. A conventional camshaft therefore turns once for those two revolutions. Cam geometry and a timing drive coordinate valve events; timing is not set by piston position alone.
parts.made: Cam surfaces, a shaft, bearings and a timed drive are manufactured and assembled.

parts.name: Spark plug & ignition
parts.simple: An ignition event initiates combustion in the charge near the chosen crank angle.
parts.deep: An ignition event initiates combustion in the charge near the chosen crank angle. Combustion then develops over time; it is not an instantaneous mechanical push. The plug and its electrical insulation serve separate functions.
parts.made: Electrodes and insulating material are retained in a sealed threaded assembly.

parts.name: Cooling & lubrication interfaces
parts.simple: Oil supplies bearing and contact interfaces while a cooling path transfers heat away from hot structures.
parts.deep: Oil supplies bearing and contact interfaces while a cooling path transfers heat away from hot structures. These systems support durability rather than directly providing the power stroke. The illustration shows interfaces, not service instructions.
parts.made: Passages, pumps, jackets, seals and heat-transfer components complete the supporting circuits.

guide.principle: The intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes occupy two crank revolutions. Gas pressure does work on the piston; the rod and crank transfer that work into shaft rotation. The ideal Otto cycle describes a thermodynamic model and is not identical to every part of a real valve-controlled cycle.
guide.design: Compression, combustion, gas exchange, friction and heat transfer interact. The slider-crank demonstration preserves the changing rod angle and piston displacement. Valve motion is illustrative rather than a manufacturer’s cam profile. Actual torque also varies through the cycle and across operating conditions.
guide.manufacture: A machined block and head locate bores, bearings and valve seats. Crank and rod assemblies require fatigue resistance and controlled fits. Rings, seals, fasteners and thermal paths turn separate parts into a durable engine.
guide.diagnosis: Separate loss of compression, ignition faults, gas-exchange restriction and friction when following the system. The experiment counts power strokes for one cylinder; it does not estimate fuel economy or engine output.
guide.equation: Single-cylinder power strokes per second = crank rpm ÷ 120
guide.history: NASA’s public Otto-cycle material explains the principle using a simple engine. The original Dialearn cutaway is a representative teaching engine, not a copied historical or production design.

experiment.label: Crankshaft speed
experiment.note: Four strokes need two crank revolutions. Count for one cylinder; no output or fuel prediction.

prediction.text: Which assembly turns the piston-and-rod motion into shaft rotation?
prediction.answer: The crank converts piston and connecting-rod motion into rotation. Main bearings locate the shaft while offset crankpins carry rod loads. The shaft must resist cyclic bending and torsion as well as transmit useful torque.

devices.description: Trace the bypass stream and the core through independently turning spools.

parts.name: Inlet & fan casing
parts.simple: The inlet presents air to the fan and the casing retains the flow path.
parts.deep: The inlet presents air to the fan and the casing retains the flow path. Distorted inlet flow can affect downstream blade loading. The cutaway removes part of the casing to expose internals without implying that an operating engine is open.
parts.made: A shaped intake and structural casing are formed and joined to the engine supports.

parts.name: Fan & low-pressure spool
parts.simple: The fan adds energy to a large air stream.
parts.deep: The fan adds energy to a large air stream. Much of that air passes around the core in a high-bypass arrangement. A shaft connects the fan to its driving turbine; the fan is not an independently powered electric propeller.
parts.made: Blades, disk, shaft and retaining features are formed, balanced and assembled.

parts.name: Core compressor
parts.simple: Successive rotating and stationary blade rows raise pressure in the core flow.
parts.deep: Successive rotating and stationary blade rows raise pressure in the core flow. Rotor work and stator flow turning serve different roles. Compressors need appropriate operating margins; more stages alone do not guarantee a better engine.
parts.made: Disks, blades and stationary vanes are precision formed and mounted in aligned cases.

parts.name: Combustor & liner
parts.simple: Fuel energy heats the compressed stream while a liner manages the reacting flow and protects surrounding structure.
parts.deep: Fuel energy heats the compressed stream while a liner manages the reacting flow and protects surrounding structure. Combustion pressure losses matter. The figure explains energy addition rather than giving fuel-delivery or operating instructions.
parts.made: A liner, casing and retained injection interfaces are fabricated and assembled.

parts.name: High-pressure turbine
parts.simple: The high-pressure turbine extracts work to drive its compressor spool.
parts.deep: The high-pressure turbine extracts work to drive its compressor spool. Its rotating rows interact with stationary nozzle guide vanes. Temperature, stress and cooling requirements differ from the fan’s colder operating environment.
parts.made: Heat-resistant blades and disks are manufactured, retained and balanced.

parts.name: Low-pressure turbine
parts.simple: A second turbine path extracts work for the fan and associated low-pressure compression.
parts.deep: A second turbine path extracts work for the fan and associated low-pressure compression. Concentric shafts allow different spool speeds. The slowed demonstration makes that speed difference visible without modelling an engine performance map.
parts.made: Turbine disks, blade rows and a separate shaft are aligned and supported.

parts.name: Bypass duct
parts.simple: The bypass path carries fan flow around the core.
parts.deep: The bypass path carries fan flow around the core. Its area and flow conditions influence the relationship between bypass and core mass flow. Bypass ratio is a mass-flow ratio rather than a ratio of visible ring diameters.
parts.made: Duct walls and structural interfaces establish a separate annular flow route.

parts.name: Concentric shafts & bearings
parts.simple: The spools transmit torque along concentric shaft paths while bearings maintain alignment.
parts.deep: The spools transmit torque along concentric shaft paths while bearings maintain alignment. The shafts must remain clear of stationary structures. Mechanical support and oil interfaces are essential even though they are less visible than blades.
parts.made: Shafts, bearings, seals and structural frames are precision manufactured and assembled.

parts.name: Exhaust nozzle
parts.simple: The nozzle converts part of the gas energy into an exiting flow.
parts.deep: The nozzle converts part of the gas energy into an exiting flow. Thrust includes momentum and pressure terms; a hot exhaust image alone does not quantify it. Core and bypass flows can leave through separate or combined arrangements.
parts.made: A shaped exhaust structure is formed with suitable thermal and structural support.

parts.name: Accessory & control system
parts.simple: Sensing and control coordinate permitted operation, while accessories support functions such as starting and lubrication.
parts.deep: Sensing and control coordinate permitted operation, while accessories support functions such as starting and lubrication. Sensor values, limits and demanded thrust interact. The control box is a representative module, not a deployable engine-control design.
parts.made: Electronics, connectors, actuators and mechanical accessory interfaces are assembled and tested.

guide.principle: A turbofan splits inlet air between a bypass path and a gas-turbine core. Compression precedes heat addition; turbine work supplies the compressor and fan; exhaust flow and bypass acceleration contribute thrust. The spools can rotate at different speeds because each has its own shaft connection.
guide.design: Fan, compressor and turbine requirements must be matched. Bypass ratio describes mass flows, not casing size. The drawing’s blade counts, shaft sizes and demonstration ratios are chosen for legibility rather than reproducing a production engine. No thrust rating is inferred from the rendered geometry.
guide.manufacture: Blade and disk manufacture, case alignment, shaft support, seals and hot-section materials all matter. An engine also needs accessory power and control. A cutaway is useful for understanding these relationships but does not depict the assembled containment structure completely.
guide.diagnosis: A loss of useful output can involve flow restriction, compression behaviour, fuel/heat addition, turbine losses or accessory faults. The interactive exercise derives bypass flow from a fixed toy core-flow value; it is not an engine sizing or flight-performance tool.
guide.equation: Bypass mass flow = bypass ratio × core mass flow
guide.history: NASA’s turbofan explanation credits the separate functions of fan, core and shafts. Many manufacturers and research teams developed modern engines; the original geometry here is not a collection figure or an OEM model.

experiment.label: Bypass ratio
experiment.note: Assume core mass flow 10 kg/s. This illustrates the definition only; it predicts no thrust.

prediction.text: Which rotating assembly adds energy to the air that later enters the bypass path?
prediction.answer: The fan adds energy to a large air stream. Much of that air passes around the core in a high-bypass arrangement. A shaft connects the fan to its driving turbine; the fan is not an independently powered electric propeller.

devices.description: Separate spacecraft orientation control from changes to its orbital path.

parts.name: Spacecraft structure
parts.simple: The bus holds equipment in known alignment.
parts.deep: The bus holds equipment in known alignment. Structural and thermal distortion can change the relationship between a sensor’s axis and an instrument’s pointing direction.
parts.made: Panels, supports and fasteners retain aligned modules.

parts.name: Reaction wheels
parts.simple: Changing wheel angular momentum produces an opposing torque on the spacecraft.
parts.deep: Changing wheel angular momentum produces an opposing torque on the spacecraft. A wheel has limited speed and momentum capacity, so repeated disturbance rejection can eventually require momentum unloading.
parts.made: Balanced wheels, motor windings and bearings form retained actuator modules.

parts.name: Guidance & control computer
parts.simple: The computer estimates the state, compares it with the requested pointing or orbit, and requests actuator actions.
parts.deep: The computer estimates the state, compares it with the requested pointing or orbit, and requests actuator actions. Sensor estimation, guidance and feedback control are related but different functions.
parts.made: Radiation-conscious electronics and interfaces are assembled onto supported boards.

parts.name: Orbit & unloading thrusters
parts.simple: A thruster exchanges momentum with expelled mass.
parts.deep: A thruster exchanges momentum with expelled mass. This can change orbit or contribute a control torque depending on location and direction. Reaction wheels alone cannot supply a sustained orbital velocity change.
parts.made: Thruster modules, valves and retained supply interfaces are fitted to structural mounts.

parts.name: Star trackers
parts.simple: A tracker observes star patterns to help establish orientation.
parts.deep: A tracker observes star patterns to help establish orientation. Its reference direction must be aligned with the spacecraft’s instrument geometry. Optical visibility and disturbances affect usable measurements.
parts.made: Optical, detector and processing assemblies are aligned in a protected housing.

parts.name: Gyroscope module
parts.simple: Gyros measure angular rate.
parts.deep: Gyros measure angular rate. Integrating a rate estimate is useful between external references, but bias accumulates into orientation error. Estimation combines complementary measurements rather than treating each sensor as perfect.
parts.made: Sensor packages and conditioning electronics are mounted in a known orientation.

parts.name: Sun sensors
parts.simple: Sun-direction measurements support orientation knowledge and appropriate operating modes.
parts.deep: Sun-direction measurements support orientation knowledge and appropriate operating modes. A direction measurement supplies different information from a full three-axis attitude solution.
parts.made: Detector elements and optical interfaces are assembled onto aligned mounts.

parts.name: Magnetic torquers
parts.simple: A controlled magnetic moment interacts with an external magnetic field to produce torque.
parts.deep: A controlled magnetic moment interacts with an external magnetic field to produce torque. Instantaneous torque cannot be chosen independently in every direction because it depends on the field direction.
parts.made: Insulated coils or retained magnetic-core assemblies are connected to drivers.

parts.name: Propulsion storage interfaces
parts.simple: Storage and delivery form part of the orbital actuator path.
parts.deep: Storage and delivery form part of the orbital actuator path. They are distinct from the wheel motor’s electrical supply. The model shows sealed modules without fuel, pressure or manoeuvre specifications.
parts.made: Sealed storage and retained delivery interfaces are assembled and qualified.

parts.name: Solar arrays & power
parts.simple: Solar cells support the electrical energy budget for sensing, computing and actuators.
parts.deep: Solar cells support the electrical energy budget for sensing, computing and actuators. Pointing, illumination and storage constraints can influence which actions remain available.
parts.made: Cells, panel structures, hinges and electrical interfaces are assembled and supported.

guide.principle: Attitude describes orientation; orbit describes motion through space. Sensors support a state estimate, guidance defines a target, and feedback requests actuator action. Wheels exchange angular momentum inside the spacecraft. Thrusters exchange momentum with expelled mass.
guide.design: Wheel saturation, sensor bias, optical visibility and actuator geometry matter. Magnetic torque depends on the local field. The drawing shows a representative spacecraft layout; its wheel axes and panel arrangement are not a mission configuration.
guide.manufacture: Aligned optical mounts, structural panels, balanced wheels and qualified electrical connections are assembled as separate modules. Thermal paths and structural stiffness help preserve calibration.
guide.diagnosis: A pointing error can originate in estimation, alignment, guidance or actuator limits. The experiment uses isolated rigid-body angular-momentum conservation and omits external torque, flexible panels and three-axis coupling.
guide.equation: Body speed change = −(wheel inertia ÷ body inertia) × wheel speed change
guide.history: ESA’s control-system and spacecraft teams describe these subsystems. Modern AOCS is a collective development in dynamics, estimation, sensors and space-qualified hardware.

experiment.label: Wheel speed change
experiment.note: Assume wheel/body inertia ratio 0.02 and zero external torque. One-axis teaching model.

prediction.text: Which actuator can change spacecraft orientation by exchanging angular momentum without firing a thruster?
prediction.answer: Changing wheel angular momentum produces an opposing torque on the spacecraft. A wheel has limited speed and momentum capacity, so repeated disturbance rejection can eventually require momentum unloading.

devices.description: Follow public heat-engine principles through separated coolant and steam loops.

parts.name: Hull & machinery supports
parts.simple: Structural supports carry the machinery and establish alignment.
parts.deep: Structural supports carry the machinery and establish alignment. The outer cutaway is context for the energy path, not a dimensional drawing of a naval vessel.
parts.made: Formed hull structures and machinery mounts retain the illustrated modules.

parts.name: Sealed reactor heat source
parts.simple: The reactor supplies heat through nuclear fission.
parts.deep: The reactor supplies heat through nuclear fission. The educational figure treats it as a sealed heat-source module and does not depict fuel construction, core configuration or operating controls.
parts.made: The illustration represents a qualified sealed assembly, without construction specifications.

parts.name: Steam generator
parts.simple: Heat crosses an exchanger from a primary coolant path into a separate water/steam path.
parts.deep: Heat crosses an exchanger from a primary coolant path into a separate water/steam path. The fluids need not mix to transfer energy.
parts.made: Pressure-retaining exchanger surfaces separate the two fluid circuits.

parts.name: Steam turbine
parts.simple: Expanding steam can transfer energy to rotating blades.
parts.deep: Expanding steam can transfer energy to rotating blades. A turbine converts part of the steam’s available energy to shaft work; exhaust steam still carries energy.
parts.made: Blade rows, a rotor and supported shaft are assembled inside a retained case.

parts.name: Condenser
parts.simple: Cooling returns exhaust steam toward liquid form so the working water can circulate again.
parts.deep: Cooling returns exhaust steam toward liquid form so the working water can circulate again. Rejecting heat is necessary to complete a practical heat-engine cycle.
parts.made: An exchanger separates the working-fluid path from its cooling path.

parts.name: Coolant & feed pumps
parts.simple: Pumps maintain appropriate circulation in the illustrated separate loops.
parts.deep: Pumps maintain appropriate circulation in the illustrated separate loops. A pump consumes shaft or electrical work; circulating fluid does not create energy.
parts.made: Impellers, housings, shafts and sealing interfaces are retained in pump assemblies.

parts.name: Drive transmission
parts.simple: The transmission carries useful shaft work toward propulsion.
parts.deep: The transmission carries useful shaft work toward propulsion. Shaft alignment, bearings and coupling behaviour remain mechanical concerns even when the heat source is nuclear.
parts.made: Shafts, bearings and coupling structures connect the power-conversion modules.

parts.name: Propulsor
parts.simple: The propulsor transfers mechanical energy to surrounding water.
parts.deep: The propulsor transfers mechanical energy to surrounding water. The representative blades explain that final conversion without specifying a vessel’s acoustic or hydrodynamic design.
parts.made: A balanced rotating assembly is retained on a supported shaft.

parts.name: Electrical generation
parts.simple: Some mechanical work can supply electrical generation for onboard loads.
parts.deep: Some mechanical work can supply electrical generation for onboard loads. Propulsion and electrical demand share the overall energy budget.
parts.made: A generator’s rotor, stator and electrical interfaces are assembled around a supported shaft.

parts.name: Monitoring interfaces
parts.simple: Instrumentation observes the plant’s condition and supports protective decisions.
parts.deep: Instrumentation observes the plant’s condition and supports protective decisions. The panel is an explanatory symbol rather than a nuclear-plant operating interface.
parts.made: Sensors, wiring and retained monitoring modules complete the public system overview.

guide.principle: Heat from a sealed nuclear source is transferred through an exchanger to a separate working-water path. Steam expansion can drive machinery; condensation and pumping close the working-fluid cycle. Useful work is only part of the heat supplied, and heat rejection is a separate necessary path.
guide.design: The primary coolant, steam/water and external cooling paths serve different roles. Their separation is important to the explanation. The figure deliberately contains no fuel parameters, reactor dimensions, tactical characteristics or operating sequence.
guide.manufacture: Retained heat-transfer surfaces, supported rotating machinery, sealed circuits and monitoring interfaces form the representative plant. The illustration conveys public energy-conversion principles, not a buildable naval design.
guide.diagnosis: Trace the heat-transfer and shaft-work paths separately. A thermal input cannot be equated directly with propulsive output. The exercise uses arbitrary energy units and a chosen conversion fraction, without modelling an actual naval plant.
guide.equation: Useful work units = supplied heat units × assumed conversion fraction
guide.history: The Department of Energy’s public naval-propulsion overview describes the separation of heat source, steam generation and propulsion machinery. The drawing is an original non-operational educational overview.

experiment.label: Assumed conversion fraction
experiment.note: Arbitrary energy units. Excludes all real naval-plant specifications and operating parameters.

prediction.text: Where does the represented propulsion system receive its initial heat input?
prediction.answer: The reactor supplies heat through nuclear fission. The educational figure treats it as a sealed heat-source module and does not depict fuel construction, core configuration or operating controls.

devices.description: Explore coordinated sensing and communication across a small civil fleet.

parts.name: Civil mission site
parts.simple: A shared site gives the fleet a reference context.
parts.deep: A shared site gives the fleet a reference context. The illustration represents surveying or inspection, not a flight plan. Physical coordinates alone do not establish safe operating permissions.
parts.made: The display platform retains the miniature aircraft and infrastructure models.

parts.name: Fleet airframes
parts.simple: Each aircraft still needs its own structure and actuators.
parts.deep: Each aircraft still needs its own structure and actuators. Swarm coordination adds another layer; it does not replace the individual flight-control and stability problem.
parts.made: Frames, motors, propellers and retained boards form each representative aircraft.

parts.name: Local flight controllers

parts.deep: Each aircraft estimates and controls its own motion. Local feedback must remain useful even when fleet communication is delayed or unavailable.

parts.name: Fleet coordination computer

parts.deep: Coordination distributes work and resolves conflicts across aircraft. A central planner and a distributed method have different communication and failure assumptions.

parts.name: Communication interfaces

parts.deep: Messages convey state and intent, but delay and loss affect how current that information is. An all-to-all network grows differently from one using local neighbours.
parts.made: Antennas, radios and retained feed interfaces connect the illustrative fleet.

parts.name: Localisation references
parts.simple: Aircraft require position or relative-state estimates.
parts.deep: Aircraft require position or relative-state estimates. Reference errors and uncertainty can affect coordination even when every motor responds correctly.

parts.name: Inspection payloads
parts.simple: Payloads gather the mission’s observations.
parts.deep: Payloads gather the mission’s observations. Sensor coverage, timing and data quality influence how tasks should be shared, rather than the fleet merely flying in a visually attractive pattern.

parts.name: Charging & docking
parts.simple: Stored energy constrains which tasks remain available.
parts.deep: Stored energy constrains which tasks remain available. Docking, recharge time and battery condition add scheduling constraints to the sensing mission.

parts.name: Human supervision interface
parts.simple: A supervising interface presents mission progress and system condition.

parts.name: Separation monitor
parts.simple: A monitor reasons about relative states and uncertainty.
parts.deep: A monitor reasons about relative states and uncertainty. Geometric distance alone does not establish a safe margin under delay, motion and sensing error. No operational collision-avoidance algorithm is supplied here.

guide.principle: Civil fleet coordination joins individually controlled aircraft with a shared task. Communication distributes observations and intent, while local control maintains each vehicle’s motion. Inspection coverage, energy availability and uncertainty create competing objectives.
guide.design: Central and distributed coordination make different assumptions about connectivity and faults. A nominal fleet shape does not demonstrate robust coordination. The 3D view shows individual rotors and shared infrastructure without prescribing real routes or flight-control gains.

guide.equation: Possible pair links = n × (n − 1) ÷ 2

parts.name: Grid site & structures
parts.simple: Structures support conductors and equipment.
parts.deep: Structures support conductors and equipment. Physical separation and retained interfaces matter independently of the software used to monitor the grid.

parts.name: Generation interface
parts.simple: Generation supplies electrical energy to the network.
parts.deep: Generation supplies electrical energy to the network. Available capacity and actual output are different quantities; changing demand must be reconciled with what the connected sources can deliver.

guide.principle: A protected battery powers a controlled actuator, which moves a supported shaft and brush head. Charging and pressure-feedback paths serve separate functions.
guide.design: Drive arrangement, head compliance, sealing and control influence the product. The oscillation is slowed for explanation and does not reproduce a commercial motor profile or provide oral-care advice.
guide.manufacture: A retained actuator, shaft supports, protected cells and sealed controls are assembled into the handle. A receiver coil completes the charging path.
guide.diagnosis: Trace power, control, motion transmission and charging separately. The exercise converts movement frequency into a count over one second rather than recommending brushing conditions.
guide.equation: Oscillations per second = frequency in hertz
guide.history: Philips describes powered brush movement and pressure feedback. The original cutaway uses an illustrative oscillator without copying a product mechanism.
